result.title: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Visual Perception in Lower-Limb Prostheses
result.comment: Accepted at IEEE International Conference on Integrated Systems in Medical Technologies 2026
result.summary: Monocular depth estimation has advanced rapidly with the development of foundation models that demonstrate strong zero-shot generalisation across diverse visual domains. However, the applicability of these models to visual perception for lower-limb prosthetics remains largely unexplored. Reliable depth perception is particularly important for prosthesis users, who often experience significant challenges when navigating stairs, uneven terrain, and other complex environments. To address this gap, we introduce the Lower-Limb Prosthesis (LP) dataset, a benchmark designed to evaluate depth perception from an emulated knee-level prosthetic viewpoint. Using this dataset, we evaluate four state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation foundation models. Our results provide the first systematic benchmark of monocular depth estimation performance from a prosthetic viewpoint, while highlighting both the challenges and the potential of deploying foundation models in prosthetic perception systems. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Ishivijay/lp_dataset.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建了模拟膝部视角的下肢假肢数据集 LP，并零样本评测四个单目深度估计基础模型在该视角下的表现，形成首个该类基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属特定应用场景的深度预测评测，未涉及 latent 推理状态、视觉证据筛选、动态计算或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的实质联系。
